requirements.quote:
Receivers send ACK frames (types 0x02 and 0x03) to inform senders of
   packets they have received and processed.  The ACK frame contains one
   or more ACK Ranges.  ACK Ranges identify acknowledged packets.  If
   the frame type is 0x03, ACK frames also contain the cumulative count
   of QUIC packets with associated ECN marks received on the connection
   up until this point.
requirements.condition: An ACK frame is encoded or decoded.
requirements.required_behavior: The frame type is 0x02 or 0x03, and the frame contains at least one ACK Range identifying acknowledged packets.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: An ACK frame must not contain zero ACK Ranges.
requirements.why_checkable: Frame type values and the number of encoded ACK ranges can be inspected directly.

requirements.quote:
the frame type is 0x03, ACK frames also contain the cumulative count
   of QUIC packets with associated ECN marks received on the connection
   up until this point.
requirements.required_behavior: The ACK frame contains cumulative ECN counts for marked QUIC packets received on the connection up to that point.
requirements.why_checkable: A type-0x03 frame can be checked for presence and values of its ECN count fields.

requirements.quote:
up until this point.  QUIC implementations MUST properly handle both
   types, and, if they have enabled ECN for packets they send, they
   SHOULD use the information in the ECN section to manage their
   congestion state.
requirements.condition: An implementation receives or processes ACK frames.
requirements.required_behavior: The implementation properly handles both ACK frame types 0x02 and 0x03.
requirements.why_checkable: Tests can supply valid frames of each type and verify that both are parsed and processed.

requirements.quote:
types, and, if they have enabled ECN for packets they send, they
   SHOULD use the information in the ECN section to manage their
   congestion state.
requirements.condition: The implementation has enabled ECN for packets it sends and processes an ACK frame containing ECN information.
requirements.required_behavior: The implementation should use the ECN information to manage its congestion state.
requirements.why_checkable: Congestion-state transitions can be observed after processing ACK ECN counts while ECN is enabled.

requirements.quote:
QUIC acknowledgments are irrevocable.  Once acknowledged, a packet
   remains acknowledged, even if it does not appear in a future ACK
   frame.
requirements.condition: A packet has been acknowledged and a later ACK frame omits that packet.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The implementation must not revoke the packet's acknowledged state because it is absent from a later ACK frame.
requirements.why_checkable: A sequence of ACK frames can verify that acknowledged state never transitions back when a later frame omits the packet.

requirements.quote:
the same numeric value.  An acknowledgment for a packet needs to
   indicate both a packet number and a packet number space.  This is
   accomplished by having each ACK frame only acknowledge packet numbers
   in the same space as the packet in which the ACK frame is contained.
requirements.condition: An ACK frame acknowledges packet numbers.
requirements.required_behavior: Every acknowledged packet number is interpreted in the packet number space of the packet containing the ACK frame.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: An ACK frame must not acknowledge packet numbers from a different packet number space than its containing packet.
requirements.why_checkable: The containing packet's number space and all packet numbers affected by ACK processing can be compared.

requirements.quote:
Version Negotiation and Retry packets cannot be acknowledged because
   they do not contain a packet number.
requirements.condition: The packet is a Version Negotiation or Retry packet.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The implementation must not acknowledge the packet using packet-number acknowledgment state or an ACK frame.
requirements.why_checkable: Tests can verify that receiving or generating ACK frames never marks Version Negotiation or Retry packets acknowledged by packet number.

requirements.quote:
frames, these packets are implicitly acknowledged by the next Initial
   packet sent by the client.
requirements.condition: A client sends the next Initial packet after a Version Negotiation or Retry packet.
requirements.required_behavior: That next client Initial packet implicitly acknowledges the Version Negotiation or Retry packet.
requirements.why_checkable: Packet-processing state can be inspected across receipt of Version Negotiation or Retry and the subsequent client Initial.

requirements.quote:
ACK Frame {
     Type (i) = 0x02..0x03,
     Largest Acknowledged (i),
     ACK Delay (i),
     ACK Range Count (i),
     First ACK Range (i),
     ACK Range (..) ...,
     [ECN Counts (..)],
   }
requirements.condition: An ACK frame is encoded or decoded.
requirements.required_behavior: Fields occur in this order: Type, Largest Acknowledged, ACK Delay, ACK Range Count, First ACK Range, zero or more additional ACK Range fields, and optional ECN Counts.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The listed fields must not be reordered.
requirements.why_checkable: The serialized field sequence can be parsed and compared with the specified grammar.

requirements.condition: The ACK frame Type field is encoded or decoded.
requirements.required_behavior: The Type field is a variable-length integer with value 0x02 or 0x03.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The Type field must not use a value outside 0x02 through 0x03 for this frame format.
requirements.why_checkable: The field encoding class and decoded numeric value are directly inspectable.

requirements.quote:
Largest Acknowledged:  A variable-length integer representing the
      largest packet number the peer is acknowledging; this is usually
      the largest packet number that the peer has received prior to
      generating the ACK frame.  Unlike the packet number in the QUIC
      long or short header, the value in an ACK frame is not truncated.
requirements.condition: The Largest Acknowledged field is encoded or decoded.
requirements.required_behavior: Encode it as a non-truncated variable-length integer representing the largest packet number acknowledged by the peer.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The value must not be encoded as a truncated packet number.
requirements.why_checkable: The decoded field value, variable-length encoding, and absence of packet-number reconstruction can be tested.

requirements.quote:
ACK Delay:  A variable-length integer encoding the acknowledgment
      delay in microseconds; see Section 13.2.5.  It is decoded by
      multiplying the value in the field by 2 to the power of the
      ack_delay_exponent transport parameter sent by the sender of the
      ACK frame; see Section 18.2.
requirements.condition: An ACK Delay field is decoded.
requirements.required_behavior: Decode the acknowledgment delay in microseconds by multiplying the variable-length integer field value by 2 raised to the ack_delay_exponent sent by the ACK frame sender.
requirements.why_checkable: Given a field value and sender-provided exponent, the resulting delay can be compared with the specified calculation.

requirements.quote:
ACK Range Count:  A variable-length integer specifying the number of
      ACK Range fields in the frame.
requirements.condition: An ACK Range Count field is encoded or decoded.
requirements.required_behavior: Encode it as a variable-length integer equal to the number of additional ACK Range fields in the frame.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The declared count must not differ from the number of ACK Range fields present.
requirements.why_checkable: The decoded count can be compared directly with the number of following ACK Range fields.

requirements.quote:
First ACK Range:  A variable-length integer indicating the number of
      contiguous packets preceding the Largest Acknowledged that are
      being acknowledged.
requirements.condition: A First ACK Range field is encoded or decoded.
requirements.required_behavior: Encode it as a variable-length integer indicating the number of contiguous acknowledged packets preceding Largest Acknowledged.
requirements.why_checkable: The field's encoding and its represented contiguous range can be checked against the acknowledged packet set.

requirements.quote:
being acknowledged.  That is, the smallest packet acknowledged in
      the range is determined by subtracting the First ACK Range value
      from the Largest Acknowledged field.
requirements.condition: The first acknowledged range is reconstructed.
requirements.required_behavior: Compute the smallest packet number in the range as Largest Acknowledged minus First ACK Range.
requirements.why_checkable: The reconstructed lower endpoint can be compared with the stated subtraction for concrete field values.

requirements.quote:
ACK Ranges:  Contains additional ranges of packets that are
      alternately not acknowledged (Gap) and acknowledged (ACK Range);
requirements.required_behavior: Interpret their components as alternating ranges of unacknowledged packets (Gap) and acknowledged packets (ACK Range).
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The Gap and ACK Range components must not be interpreted in a non-alternating order.
requirements.why_checkable: A parsed sequence can be inspected to verify alternating gap and acknowledged-range semantics.

requirements.quote: ECN Counts:  The three ECN counts; see Section 19.3.2.
requirements.condition: The ECN Counts section is present.
requirements.required_behavior: The section contains exactly three ECN counts.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The section must not contain a number of ECN counts other than three.
requirements.why_checkable: The number of decoded ECN count values is directly countable.
